records.source: וַתֹּ֥אמֶר לָ֖הּ נָעֳמִ֣י חֲמוֹתָ֑הּ בִּתִּ֞י הֲלֹ֧א אֲבַקֶּשׁ־לָ֛ךְ מָנ֖וֹחַ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִֽיטַב־לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And said to her Naomi her mother-in-law, my daughter, shall I not seek for you a resting place that it may go well for you?
pieces: Naomi, her mother-in-law, said to her, "My daughter, is it not time I looked for a settled home for you, where your life will go well?

L.1: And Naomi her mother-in-law said to her, "My daughter, should I not seek a resting place for you, so that it may go well with you?

R.1: One day Naomi said to Ruth, "My daughter, I want to find a husband and a home for you, where you will be safe and cared for.

decisions.choice: a resting place: a settled home in marriage
decisions.reason: The word means a place of rest, a secure home. Naomi has already prayed that each of her daughters-in-law would find rest "in the house of her husband" (1:9), with a word from the same root. Now she sets out to bring that about for Ruth.

decisions.choice: should I not seek: a question that expects yes
decisions.reason: The question is a way of saying "I must". Naomi speaks as the older woman responsible for her widowed daughter-in-law; in that world a marriage was arranged by the family, not by the bride alone.

decisions.choice: a husband and a home ... safe and cared for
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the resting place is (decision m1) and turns the question that expects yes into a statement of what Naomi wants. "Ruth" is named for "her".

records.heading: Ruth at the threshing floor

records.source: וְעַתָּ֗ה הֲלֹ֥א בֹ֨עַז֙ מֹֽדַעְתָּ֔נוּ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיִ֖ית אֶת־נַעֲרוֹתָ֑יו הִנֵּה־ה֗וּא זֹרֶ֛ה אֶת־גֹּ֥רֶן הַשְּׂעֹרִ֖ים הַלָּֽיְלָה׃
records.gloss: And now, [is] not Boaz our relative, with whose young women you were? Look, he [is] winnowing the threshing floor of the barley tonight.
pieces: Now Boaz, whose young women you have been working with, is our relative, is he not? Tonight he is winnowing barley on the threshing floor.

L.2: And now, is not Boaz our relative, whose young women you were with? Look, he is winnowing [at] the threshing floor of the barley tonight.

R.2: You know that Boaz is one of our relatives, and you have been working with his young women. Tonight he will be at the threshing floor, winnowing barley. He will toss the grain into the air so the wind can blow the husks away.

decisions.choice: our relative: a member of the family circle
decisions.reason: The word names a relative or close acquaintance. Naomi has already told Ruth that Boaz is one of their redeemers (2:20; see also 2:1). Saying "our" relative, she includes Ruth in the family.

decisions.choice: winnowing at night: separating grain from chaff in the evening breeze
decisions.reason: After threshing, the grain and chaff were thrown into the air with a fork so the wind carried off the light chaff while the heavy grain fell back. The evening breeze was used for the work. The threshing floor was a hard, open place outside the town (verse 15 says Boaz then went into the town), and the owner and workers often slept there to guard the grain.

decisions.choice: He will toss the grain into the air so the wind can blow the husks away.
decisions.reason: Readable explains what winnowing is, since many readers will not know the word. It turns Naomi's question that expects yes into a statement.

records.source: וְרָחַ֣צְתְּ׀וָסַ֗כְתְּ וְשַׂ֧מְתְּ שִׂמְלֹתַ֛יִךְ עָלַ֖יִךְ וְיָרַ֣דְתְּ הַגֹּ֑רֶן אַל־תִּוָּדְעִ֣י לָאִ֔ישׁ עַ֥ד כַּלֹּת֖וֹ לֶאֱכֹ֥ל וְלִשְׁתּֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And you will wash and anoint yourself and put your garments on you, and go down [to] the threshing floor; do not make yourself known to the man until he finishes eating and drinking.
pieces: So bathe, put on perfumed oil, dress yourself well, and go down to the threshing floor. But keep out of the man's sight until his eating and drinking are over.

L.3: So wash and anoint yourself, and put your garments on, and go down to the threshing floor; do not let yourself be known to the man until he has finished eating and drinking.

R.3: Take a bath, put on perfume, and dress in your best clothes. Then go down to the threshing floor, but stay where he cannot see you until he has finished eating and drinking.

decisions.choice: your garments ... you will go down: the readings of the margin (qere)
alternatives: and I will go down (the written text, read as Naomi's words about herself)
decisions.reason: Two words in this verse are written one way and read another. The written text (ketiv) has "your garment", one garment, perhaps an outer cloak; the margin (qere) reads "your garments". The written text also has a form that looks like "and I will go down"; the margin reads "and you will go down". The written form is most likely an older spelling of the "you" form for a woman, which the margin brings up to date, since Ruth goes down alone (verse 6) and Naomi stays at home (verse 16). The margin is followed in both places.

decisions.choice: wash, anoint, put on garments: making ready, perhaps putting off mourning
decisions.reason: Washing, rubbing the skin with scented oil and putting on clothes are the steps David takes when his time of mourning ends (2 Samuel 12:20), and those a bride's adornment is described with (Ezekiel 16:9-10). Ruth, a widow, is to make herself ready to present herself as a woman free to marry.

decisions.choice: do not make yourself known: keep out of sight until he has eaten
decisions.reason: Ruth is to wait until Boaz has had his meal and lies down (verse 4). She is not to be seen by the man while the workers are about, and the request comes when he is alone and at ease (verse 7).

decisions.choice: dress yourself well / dress in your best clothes
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "put your garments on you", kept at Literal. Coming after the washing and the oil, it means dressing with care (decision m2), which Balanced and Readable say.

records.source: וִיהִ֣י בְשָׁכְב֗וֹ וְיָדַ֨עַתְּ֙ אֶת־הַמָּקוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִשְׁכַּב־שָׁ֔ם וּבָ֛את וְגִלִּ֥ית מַרְגְּלֹתָ֖יו וְשָׁכָ֑בְתְּ וְהוּא֙ יַגִּ֣יד לָ֔ךְ אֵ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּעַשִֽׂין׃
records.gloss: And let it be when he lies down, and you will know the place where he lies there, and you will go in and uncover his feet and lie down; and he will tell you what you will do.
pieces: When he lies down, mark the spot where he is lying. Then go to him, uncover his feet and lie down there, and he will tell you what you should do."

L.4: And when he lies down, take note of the place where he lies; then go in and uncover his feet and lie down, and he will tell you what you are to do."

R.4: Watch to see where he lies down to sleep. Then go to him, uncover his feet by turning back his cloak, and lie down there. He will let you know what to do next."

decisions.choice: uncover his feet: turn back the covering from the place of his feet
alternatives: uncover the place of his legs
a veiled way of saying she is to offer herself to him
decisions.reason: The word for "feet" here is not the common one; it means the place of the feet, the area at a sleeper's feet and legs (the same word comes in Daniel 10:6 for the legs). Ruth is to fold back Boaz's cloak there and lie down at his feet, the place of a servant. It is a silent request that he will understand when he wakes. "Feet" can be a modest way of naming the private parts elsewhere (Isaiah 7:20), and the words "lie down", "know" and "uncover" can all carry a sexual sense, so the scene is told with tension. But the story shows nothing improper happening: Boaz praises Ruth as a woman of worth (verse 11), keeps her safe till morning, and protects her name (verse 14).

decisions.choice: and lie down: the reading of the margin (qere)
alternatives: and I will lie down (the written text)
decisions.reason: As with "go down" in verse 3, the written text has a form that looks like "and I will lie down"; the margin reads "and you will lie down". The written form is most likely the older spelling of the "you" form for a woman, and the margin is followed.

decisions.choice: he will tell you what you are to do: Boaz is to answer
decisions.reason: Naomi leaves the next step to Boaz. In the event Ruth speaks first and tells him what she asks (verse 9), and he answers (verses 10-13).

decisions.choice: by turning back his cloak
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the picture of uncovering his feet and says what the act was (decision m1), so that the reader does not imagine something else.

records.source: וַתֹּ֖אמֶר אֵלֶ֑יהָ כֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־תֹּאמְרִ֥י אֵלַ֖י אֶֽעֱשֶֽׂה׃
records.gloss: And she said to her, all that you say to me I will do.
pieces: Ruth answered her, "I will do everything you tell me."

L.5: And she said to her, "All that you say to me I will do."

R.5: Ruth said, "I will do everything you say."

decisions.choice: to me: read in the margin (qere) though not written
decisions.reason: The words "to me" are not written in the text; the margin tells the reader to say them. They make no difference to the meaning. The same happens in verse 17.

decisions.choice: all that you say I will do
decisions.reason: Ruth's answer is matched by Boaz's words to her in verse 11, "all that you say I will do for you". She trusts Naomi; Boaz will keep faith with Ruth.

decisions.choice: Ruth
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker, since "she" and "her" are both women.

records.source: וַתֵּ֖רֶד הַגֹּ֑רֶן וַתַּ֕עַשׂ כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־צִוַּ֖תָּה חֲמוֹתָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And she went down [to] the threshing floor and did according to all that had commanded her her mother-in-law.
pieces: So she went down to the threshing floor and did exactly as her mother-in-law had instructed her.

L.6: So she went down to the threshing floor and did according to all that her mother-in-law had commanded her.

R.6: So Ruth went down to the threshing floor and did just what her mother-in-law had told her.

decisions.choice: did according to all: a summary told first
decisions.reason: The verse sums up what follows: verse 7 tells how she carried out each step. In fact she goes one step further than Naomi said, by speaking first (verse 9).

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אכַל בֹּ֤עַז וַיֵּשְׁתְּ֙ וַיִּיטַ֣ב לִבּ֔וֹ וַיָּבֹ֕א לִשְׁכַּ֖ב בִּקְצֵ֣ה הָעֲרֵמָ֑ה וַתָּבֹ֣א בַלָּ֔ט וַתְּגַ֥ל מַרְגְּלֹתָ֖יו וַתִּשְׁכָּֽב׃
records.gloss: And ate Boaz and drank, and was good his heart, and he went to lie down at [the] end of the heap; and she came in secret and uncovered his feet and lay down.
pieces: Boaz ate and drank and was in a happy mood. He went off and lay down at the far end of the grain pile, and she came quietly, uncovered his feet, and lay down.

L.7: And Boaz ate and drank, and his heart was good, and he went to lie down at the end of the grain heap. Then she came quietly and uncovered his feet and lay down.

R.7: Boaz ate and drank, and he felt happy and content. Then he went to sleep at the far end of the pile of grain. Ruth came quietly, uncovered his feet by turning back his cloak, and lay down there.

decisions.choice: his heart was good: he was cheerful and content
decisions.reason: "His heart was good" means he was in good spirits after the meal (Judges 19:6; 1 Kings 21:7). It does not say he was drunk; the harvest meal ends a good day's work, and Boaz is clear-headed when he wakes (verses 10-13).

decisions.choice: at the end of the grain heap: guarding the harvest
decisions.reason: The owner slept beside the heap of winnowed grain to guard it through the night. The edge of the heap was away from the others, which let Ruth come to him unseen.

decisions.choice: quietly ... uncovered his feet
decisions.reason: The word means secretly or softly, without being noticed (1 Samuel 18:22; 24:5). She does just what Naomi said (verse 4); see the decision there on uncovering his feet.

records.source: וַיְהִי֙ בַּחֲצִ֣י הַלַּ֔יְלָה וַיֶּחֱרַ֥ד הָאִ֖ישׁ וַיִּלָּפֵ֑ת וְהִנֵּ֣ה אִשָּׁ֔ה שֹׁכֶ֖בֶת מַרְגְּלֹתָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And it was in [the] middle of the night, and trembled the man and turned himself, and there, a woman lying [at] his feet.
pieces: In the middle of the night the man woke with a start and turned over. A woman was lying at his feet!

L.8: And it happened at midnight that the man was startled and turned himself, and there was a woman lying at his feet!

R.8: In the middle of the night Boaz suddenly woke up. He turned over and was surprised to find a woman lying at his feet.

decisions.choice: startled and turned himself: he woke with a start and turned or bent forward
alternatives: he bent forward (to feel what was there)
decisions.reason: The first verb means to tremble or start in fear or surprise. The second means to twist, turn or bend; Judges 16:29 uses it of Samson taking hold of the pillars. Boaz may have shivered with the cold at his uncovered feet, then turned over or leaned forward to see.

decisions.choice: there was a woman: seen through Boaz's eyes
decisions.reason: The word "there" (hinneh) takes the reader into Boaz's surprise. In the dark he sees only that a woman is lying there; he does not yet know who she is (verse 9).

decisions.choice: Boaz
decisions.reason: Readable names "the man" as Boaz, as verse 7 has.

records.source: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר מִי־אָ֑תּוַתֹּ֗אמֶר אָנֹכִי֙ ר֣וּת אֲמָתֶ֔ךָ וּפָרַשְׂתָּ֤ כְנָפֶ֨ךָ֙ עַל־אֲמָ֣תְךָ֔ כִּ֥י גֹאֵ֖ל אָֽתָּה׃
records.gloss: And he said, who [are] you? And she said, I [am] Ruth your maidservant, and you will spread your wing over your maidservant, for a redeemer you [are].
pieces: "Who are you?" he asked. She answered, "I am Ruth, your servant. Spread the wing of your cloak over your servant, for you are a family redeemer."

L.9: And he said, "Who are you?" And she said, "I am Ruth, your maidservant. Spread your wing over your maidservant, for you are a redeemer."

R.9: "Who are you?" he asked. She answered, "I am Ruth, your servant. Cover me with the corner of your cloak to show that you will marry me and take care of me. You are one of our family redeemers."

decisions.choice: spread your wing over: take me as your wife and under your protection
decisions.reason: The word means a wing, and also the corner or edge of a garment. Spreading the corner of one's garment over a woman was a sign of taking her as wife (Ezekiel 16:8, where God says "I spread my wing over you ... and you became mine"; compare Deuteronomy 23:1). Boaz had prayed that Ruth would find a full reward from the LORD, "under whose wings you have come to take refuge" (2:12). Now she asks Boaz himself to be the answer to that prayer.

decisions.choice: your maidservant: a woman who could become a wife
decisions.reason: In 2:13 Ruth called herself by a humbler word for a servant girl, one not even counted among his servants. Here she uses another word for a female servant, one used of women who could be taken as wives (as Hagar and Bilhah, Genesis 21:10; 30:3). She speaks humbly, but as one who may marry him.

decisions.choice: you are a redeemer: the reason for her request
decisions.reason: The redeemer (go'el) was the close relative bound to buy back family land and care for the family line (2:20; Leviticus 25:25). The law gave the duty of marrying a dead man's widow to his brother (Deuteronomy 25:5-10), not to the redeemer. Ruth joins the two duties: she asks Boaz, as redeemer, to marry her and keep her dead husband's family alive. Boaz accepts that this goes together (verses 12-13), and so does the town (4:5, 10).

decisions.choice: the wing of your cloak
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the word "wing", so that the link with 2:12 can be seen, and adds "of your cloak" to show that a garment is meant. Literal keeps "your wing" alone.

decisions.choice: to show that you will marry me and take care of me ... one of our family redeemers
decisions.reason: Readable says what the gesture meant (decision m1) and names the family the redeemer acts for (decision m3). It says "one of our family redeemers", as Naomi did (2:20), because a nearer redeemer exists (verse 12).

decisions.choice: family redeemer
decisions.reason: "Family redeemer" at Balanced and Readable, "redeemer" at Literal, as throughout Ruth (2:20), so that the reader sees a relative's duty is meant, not salvation from sin.

records.source: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר בְּרוּכָ֨ה אַ֤תְּ לַֽיהוָה֙ בִּתִּ֔י הֵיטַ֛בְתְּ חַסְדֵּ֥ךְ הָאַחֲר֖וֹן מִן־הָרִאשׁ֑וֹן לְבִלְתִּי־לֶ֗כֶת אַחֲרֵי֙ הַבַּ֣חוּרִ֔ים אִם־דַּ֖ל וְאִם־עָשִֽׁיר׃
records.gloss: And he said, blessed [are] you by YHWH, my daughter; you have made good your latter steadfast love more than the first, by not going after the young men, whether poor or rich.
pieces: He said, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} bless you, my daughter! This faithful love you have shown now is greater than what you showed before, since you have not looked to the young men for a husband, whether poor or rich.

L.10: And he said, "Blessed are you by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, my daughter! You have made this latter steadfast love better than the first, by not going after the young men, whether poor or rich.

R.10: Boaz said, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} bless you, my daughter! You showed faithful love to Naomi before, and now you are showing even greater faithful love. You could have tried to marry a younger man, rich or poor, but you did not.

decisions.choice: steadfast love: loyalty and kindness beyond what duty asks
decisions.reason: The word (chesed) means loyal, faithful love, kindness that keeps faith with those one is bound to and goes beyond what is owed. It is the word Naomi used when she prayed for her daughters-in-law (1:8) and the word for the LORD's love in Exodus 34:6.

decisions.choice: the latter better than the first: two acts of loyalty
alternatives: the first: her kindness to her dead husband (1:8)
decisions.reason: The first act of faithful love is most likely Ruth's leaving her own land to care for Naomi (2:11; 1:16-17). The latter is this night's request: instead of choosing a husband for herself, she has asked the family's redeemer to marry her, so that her dead husband's name and Naomi's family line may go on (4:10).

decisions.choice: not going after the young men: not looking for a husband of her own age
decisions.reason: "Going after" a man means seeking him as a husband. Boaz's words suggest he is older than Ruth. "Whether poor or rich" means any young man at all: she was free to look for love or for wealth, and chose family loyalty instead.

decisions.choice: steadfast love (Literal); faithful love (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The word is rendered as in Exodus 34:6 and Deuteronomy: "steadfast love" at Literal, "faithful love" at Balanced and Readable, which shows both the loyalty and the warmth of the word.

decisions.choice: to Naomi before
decisions.reason: Readable names Naomi as the one Ruth first showed faithful love to (decision m2), and puts "going after the young men" as trying to marry a younger man (decision m3).

decisions.choice: looked to the young men for a husband
decisions.reason: Balanced says what "going after" the young men means (decision m3).

records.source: וְעַתָּ֗ה בִּתִּי֙ אַל־תִּ֣ירְאִ֔י כֹּ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־תֹּאמְרִ֖י אֶֽעֱשֶׂה־לָּ֑ךְ כִּ֤י יוֹדֵ֨עַ֙ כָּל־שַׁ֣עַר עַמִּ֔י כִּ֛י אֵ֥שֶׁת חַ֖יִל אָֽתְּ׃
records.gloss: And now, my daughter, do not fear; all that you say I will do for you, for knows all [the] gate of my people that a woman of worth you [are].
pieces: So now, my daughter, have no fear. Whatever you ask, I will do for you. The whole town knows you are a woman of real worth.

L.11: And now, my daughter, do not be afraid. All that you say I will do for you, for all the gate of my people knows that you are a woman of worth.

R.11: Now, my daughter, do not be afraid. I will do everything you ask. All the people in our town know that you are a fine woman of good character.

decisions.choice: all the gate of my people: everyone in the town
decisions.reason: The gate of a town was where its people met, where business was done and where the elders settled cases (4:1, 11). "All the gate of my people" means the whole town, all who gather there.

decisions.choice: a woman of worth: strong, capable and good
decisions.reason: The phrase (eshet chayil) joins "woman" with a word for strength, ability and worth. It is the phrase of Proverbs 31:10 and 12:4. The same word chayil described Boaz, "a man mighty in wealth" (2:1): Ruth is his equal in character, though she is a poor foreigner.

decisions.choice: all that you say I will do for you
decisions.reason: Boaz answers Ruth with the very words she gave Naomi (verse 5).

decisions.choice: ask
decisions.reason: "Say" here means what Ruth has asked of him, so Balanced and Readable say "ask". Literal keeps "say" to show the echo of verse 5.

records.source: וְעַתָּה֙ כִּ֣י אָמְנָ֔ם כִּ֥י גֹאֵ֖ל אָנֹ֑כִי וְגַ֛ם יֵ֥שׁ גֹּאֵ֖ל קָר֥וֹב מִמֶּֽנִּי׃
records.gloss: And now, truly that [if] a redeemer I [am], and also there is a redeemer nearer than I.
pieces: It is true that I am a family redeemer, but there is a family redeemer more closely related than I am.

L.12: And now, truly I am a redeemer; and yet there is a redeemer nearer than I.

R.12: It is true that I am a family redeemer. But there is another man who is a closer relative than I am, and he has the first right to redeem you.

decisions.choice: it is true that: a written word is left unread
alternatives: truly, if I am a redeemer (with the written word)
decisions.reason: After "that" the written text (ketiv) has a further word, "if", which the reading tradition (qere) tells the reader to leave out. Read with it, the words would be an unusual way of saying "truly that"; read without it, "it is true that". The sense is the same, and the reading tradition is followed.

decisions.choice: a redeemer nearer than I: the closer relative has the first right
decisions.reason: The duty and right to redeem passed to the nearest relative first, and then to the next (Leviticus 25:25, 48-49). Boaz is willing, but he will not set aside the right of the closer relative; chapter 4 tells how the matter is settled at the town gate (4:1-10).

decisions.choice: and he has the first right to redeem you
decisions.reason: Readable says what "nearer" means for Ruth (decision m2).

records.source: לִ֣ינִי׀הַלַּ֗יְלָה וְהָיָ֤ה בַבֹּ֨קֶר֙ אִם־יִגְאָלֵ֥ךְ טוֹב֙ יִגְאָ֔ל וְאִם־לֹ֨א יַחְפֹּ֧ץ לְגָֽאֳלֵ֛ךְ וּגְאַלְתִּ֥יךְ אָנֹ֖כִי חַי־יְהוָ֑ה שִׁכְבִ֖י עַד־הַבֹּֽקֶר׃
records.gloss: Stay the night, and it will be in the morning, if he will redeem you, good, let him redeem; and if he is not willing to redeem you, then I will redeem you, I, [as] YHWH lives. Lie down until the morning.
pieces: Stay here for the night. In the morning, if he will act as redeemer for you, well and good: let him do it. But if he does not want to redeem you, then as surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, I will redeem you myself. Lie down here until morning."

L.13: Stay the night, and in the morning, if he will redeem you, good, let him redeem; but if he is not willing to redeem you, then I will redeem you, I myself, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives. Lie down until the morning."

R.13: Stay here tonight. In the morning, if he is willing to redeem you, that is fine; let him do it. But if he does not want to, then I promise you, as surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, I will do it myself. Now lie down here until morning."

decisions.choice: redeem you: take responsibility for you and your family's land and line
decisions.reason: Here "redeem" means more than buying land: it means taking Ruth as wife and caring for Elimelech's family, its land and its name, as chapter 4 shows (4:5, 10).

decisions.choice: as the LORD lives: an oath
decisions.reason: Boaz binds himself with an oath by the life of the LORD. He does not leave Ruth with a vague hope: if the nearer relative will not act, Boaz will.

decisions.choice: stay the night ... lie down until the morning: for her safety
decisions.reason: Boaz does not send Ruth home through the dark, where she could be harmed or seen (compare 2:22). She is to stay where she is until it is nearly light (verse 14).

decisions.choice: good, let him redeem
decisions.reason: The word means "good": that would be well. It is not a name, though some have read it as one ("if Tob will redeem you").

decisions.choice: act as redeemer for you
decisions.reason: Balanced says "act as redeemer for you" the first time, so the reader takes "redeem" as a relative's duty (decision m1); after that it says "redeem".

records.source: וַתִּשְׁכַּ֤ב מַרְגְּלוֹתָיוֹ֙עַד־הַבֹּ֔קֶר וַתָּ֕קָם בְּטֶ֛רֶם יַכִּ֥יר אִ֖ישׁ אֶת־רֵעֵ֑הוּ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אַל־יִוָּדַ֔ע כִּי־בָ֥אָה הָאִשָּׁ֖ה הַגֹּֽרֶן׃
records.gloss: And she lay [at] his feet until the morning, and she rose before could recognize a man his neighbor; and he said, let it not be known that came the woman [to] the threshing floor.
pieces: So she lay at his feet until morning, but she got up before it was light enough for anyone to recognize another. And he said, "It must not be known that the woman came to the threshing floor."

L.14: And she lay at his feet until morning, and she rose while it was still too early for one to recognize another. And he said, "May it not be known that the woman came to the threshing floor."

R.14: So Ruth lay at his feet until morning. She got up while it was still too dark for people to see who anyone was. Boaz said, "No one must find out that a woman came to the threshing floor."

decisions.choice: his feet; before: the readings of the margin (qere)
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) and the reading the scribes marked (qere) are two spellings of the same words, "his feet" and "before". The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: let it not be known: to guard her name
decisions.reason: A woman found at night at a threshing floor would be suspected of selling herself, since harvest time and threshing floors were linked with that (Hosea 9:1). Boaz protects Ruth's good name, and keeps the matter quiet until it is settled with the nearer redeemer.

decisions.choice: he said: to Ruth, or to himself
decisions.reason: The verse does not say whom Boaz spoke to. He may have said it to Ruth as she left, or to himself, as "said" can mean thought (Genesis 20:11). The meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: one ... another / anyone ... another / anyone
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "a man his neighbor", an idiom for one person and another; it is not about men only. Every level says so in words that are already inclusive.

decisions.choice: Boaz
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker.

records.source: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הָ֠בִי הַמִּטְפַּ֧חַת אֲשֶׁר־עָלַ֛יִךְ וְאֶֽחֳזִי־בָ֖הּ וַתֹּ֣אחֶז בָּ֑הּ וַיָּ֤מָד שֵׁשׁ־שְׂעֹרִים֙ וַיָּ֣שֶׁת עָלֶ֔יהָ וַיָּבֹ֖א הָעִֽיר׃
records.gloss: And he said, bring the shawl that [is] on you and hold it; and she held it, and he measured six [of] barley and put [it] on her; and he went [into] the city.
pieces: Then he said, "Hand me the shawl you have on and hold it out." When she held it out, he measured six measures of barley into it and set the load on her. Then he went into the town.

L.15: And he said, "Give [me] the shawl that is on you, and take hold of it." And she took hold of it, and he measured six [measures of] barley and laid [it] on her. Then he went into the town.

R.15: Boaz said, "Bring me the shawl you are wearing and hold it open." She held it open, and he poured six measures of barley into it and put the load on her to carry. Then Boaz went back to town.

decisions.choice: six of barley: six measures of an unnamed size
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "six of barley" and does not name the measure. Six ephahs (about 120 quarts) would be far too much for one woman to carry; six seahs (a seah is a third of an ephah) would still be very heavy. The measure may have been a smaller scoop or the like. All that is certain is that it was a generous gift that Ruth could carry.

decisions.choice: shawl: a wide cloak or wrap
decisions.reason: The word names a large wrap or mantle worn by women (Isaiah 3:22). Held out, it could hold a heavy load of grain.

decisions.choice: he went into the town: the received text
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text says "he went", that is Boaz went into the town. Some Hebrew manuscripts and ancient translations read "she went", which fits the next verse, where Ruth comes to Naomi. The received text is followed; both are true in the story, since Boaz goes to the town gate (4:1) and Ruth goes home.

decisions.choice: six [measures of] barley / six measures of barley
decisions.reason: English needs a word for the unit, so "measures" is supplied (in brackets at Literal). No modern measure is given, since the Hebrew does not say which unit is meant (decision m1).

decisions.choice: town
decisions.reason: The word can mean a city or a town; Bethlehem was a small town, so every level says "town", as in 1:19 and 2:18.

records.source: וַתָּבוֹא֙ אֶל־חֲמוֹתָ֔הּ וַתֹּ֖אמֶר מִי־אַ֣תְּ בִּתִּ֑י וַתַּ֨גֶּד־לָ֔הּ אֵ֛ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָֽשָׂה־לָ֖הּ הָאִֽישׁ׃
records.gloss: And she came to her mother-in-law, and she said, who [are] you, my daughter? And she told her all that had done for her the man.
pieces: When she came to her mother-in-law, Naomi said, "How do things stand with you, my daughter?" Then Ruth told her everything the man had done for her.

L.16: And she came to her mother-in-law, and she said, "Who are you, my daughter?" And she told her all that the man had done for her.

R.16: When Ruth came home, her mother-in-law asked, "My daughter, how are things for you now?" Then Ruth told her everything that Boaz had done for her.

decisions.choice: who are you: how do you stand now?
alternatives: are you my daughter? (Naomi did not recognize her in the half-dark)
decisions.reason: Naomi is not asking Ruth's name. The question asks about her state: what has she become this night? Is she to be a bride? The same words are Boaz's question in the dark (verse 9), where he asks who she is.

decisions.choice: Naomi; Ruth; Boaz
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speakers, since both women are "she"; Readable also names "the man".

records.source: וַתֹּ֕אמֶר שֵׁשׁ־הַשְּׂעֹרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה נָ֣תַן לִ֑י כִּ֚י אָמַ֣ר אֵלַ֔י אַל־תָּב֥וֹאִי רֵיקָ֖ם אֶל־חֲמוֹתֵֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And she said, these six [of] barley he gave to me, for he said to me, do not go empty to your mother-in-law.
pieces: She said, "He gave me these six measures of barley. 'Do not go back to your mother-in-law empty-handed,' he told me."

L.17: And she said, "These six [measures of] barley he gave to me, for he said to me, 'Do not go empty to your mother-in-law.'"

R.17: Ruth said, "He gave me these six measures of barley. He told me, 'Do not go home to your mother-in-law with nothing.'"

decisions.choice: empty: the word of Naomi's grief
decisions.reason: Naomi had said, "I went away full, and the LORD has brought me back empty" (1:21). The gift, and Boaz's words about it, tell her that her emptiness is beginning to be filled. Only Ruth's report gives these words of Boaz.

decisions.choice: to me: read in the margin (qere) though not written
decisions.reason: As in verse 5, the words "to me" are not written in the text but are read; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: empty-handed / with nothing
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "empty-handed" and "with nothing", which is what "empty" means here. Literal keeps "empty", so the echo of 1:21 can be seen.

records.source: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ שְׁבִ֣י בִתִּ֔י עַ֚ד אֲשֶׁ֣ר תֵּֽדְעִ֔ין אֵ֖יךְ יִפֹּ֣ל דָּבָ֑ר כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יִשְׁקֹט֙ הָאִ֔ישׁ כִּֽי־אִם־כִּלָּ֥ה הַדָּבָ֖ר הַיּֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: And she said, sit, my daughter, until you know how will fall [the] matter, for will not rest the man unless he has finished the matter today.
pieces: Naomi said, "Stay here quietly, my daughter, until you know how things fall out. The man will not rest until he has brought the matter to an end today."

L.18: And she said, "Sit [still], my daughter, until you know how the matter will fall, for the man will not rest unless he has finished the matter today."

R.18: Naomi said, "Be patient, my daughter, and see how it all ends. Boaz will not take any rest today until he has dealt with this."

decisions.choice: sit; how the matter will fall: wait and see how it turns out
decisions.reason: "Sit" means stay quietly and wait. "How a matter falls" means how it turns out. Ruth has done her part; the rest is in Boaz's hands.

decisions.choice: he will not rest unless he has finished it today
decisions.reason: Naomi is sure Boaz will act at once. The next chapter bears her out: he goes straight to the town gate (4:1).

decisions.choice: Stay here quietly / Be patient; fall out / ends
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "sit" and "fall" mean (decision m1); Literal keeps the Hebrew picture.
